openSource.description: Fast, non-autoregressive System 1 LLM decision engine
openSource.details: Laya is a fast, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine that uses sub-billion-parameter models with calibrated probabilities to route tasks and detect intent.

contributions.title: Local CLI and FastAPI Demo Server
contributions.whatIDid: Built a production-ready FastAPI server for testing the decision engine's routing locally. Removed the global thread lock to allow concurrent requests, added Python __main__ entry points for CLI use, added a [server] dependency group to pyproject.toml and covered it all with GitHub Actions CI.
contributions.whyIDidIt: Laya had no dedicated server for testing routing pipelines, so users relied on slow, synchronous local scripts, and a global thread lock blocked concurrent requests.
contributions.whyIChooseThis: FastAPI gives an async-first, highly concurrent backend, so engineers can test the decision engine quickly before deploying.

commits.message: feat: add CLI and FastAPI demo server
fix: address Copilot code review feedback

contributions.title: Cross-Lingual Calibration
contributions.whatIDid: Added JSON-based, per-language temperature calibration to the PyTorch inference pipeline (laya.load). Wrote a script that fits maximum-likelihood temperatures on the MASSIVE validation splits to reduce Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Fixed a bug where language-specific parameters bypassed the temperature clamping bounds, and extended the pytest suite (test_laya_eval.py) to verify the temperature routing logic.
contributions.whyIDidIt: The evaluation head was overconfident on non-English languages such as Chinese, which made cross-lingual confidence scores unreliable.
contributions.whyIChooseThis: Fitting temperatures per language and applying them inside the inference pipeline fixes the miscalibration at its source, giving consistent confidence scores across all supported languages.

commits.message: feat: add lang_temperatures and fix shadowing bug

contributions.title: Email Parsing & Disclaimer Sanitization
contributions.whatIDid: Fixed a bug where clean_email_body silently deleted unpunctuated user requests that shared a paragraph with a corporate disclaimer. Added a regex lookahead (_FRESH_NEWLINE = re.compile(r"\n\s*(?=[A-Z])")) that separates wrapped boilerplate from the actual request.
contributions.whyIDidIt: Corporate emails often append disclaimers directly to the user's message. The parser was throwing that text away, causing many missed intent detections.
contributions.whyIChooseThis: A regex lookahead runs in linear time with no NLP overhead, so it fixes the data loss without affecting the engine's sub-millisecond latency.

commits.message: fix(email): recover the request when a disclaimer shares its paragraph

openSource.description: High-throughput and memory-efficient LLM serving engine
openSource.details: vLLM is a fast, easy-to-use library for LLM inference and serving, known for its high throughput and memory efficiency through PagedAttention.

contributions.title: Tensor Parallel (TP) Mixture of Experts (MoE) Optimization
contributions.whatIDid: Optimized collective operations for Mixture of Experts (MoE) models running with Tensor Parallelism (TP), using torch.compile.
contributions.whyIDidIt: Under high concurrency, MoE models saw latency spikes from unoptimized collective operations across tensor-parallel shards.
contributions.whyIChooseThis: torch.compile enables kernel fusion and graph-level optimization, improving throughput on NVIDIA GPUs.

commits.message: Optimized collectives in Tensor Parallel (TP) MoE using torch.compile

contributions.title: Hybrid Model KV Cache Sizing Fix
contributions.whatIDid: Fixed the KV cache group sizing logic for arbitrary hybrid models so they stay within memory during inference.
contributions.whyIDidIt: Hybrid model architectures were hitting out-of-memory (OOM) errors because the engine miscalculated their KV cache block requirements.
contributions.whyIChooseThis: I refactored the sizing logic to read each model's head configuration at runtime, so new hybrid architectures are sized correctly too.

commits.message: Fixed KV cache group sizing logic for arbitrary hybrid models
